newsitem.title: GERMANY: DMG raises loss forecast for Holzmann.
newsitem.headline: DMG raises loss forecast for Holzmann.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfall said on Tuesday it had revised its loss per share forecast sharply higher for troubled construction firm Philip Holzmann AG.

DMG, the research arm of Deutsche Bank, said it had increased its 1996 loss per share forecast to 31.10 marks, from 13.60 marks and its 1997 loss forecast to 57.20 marks from 1.30 marks. For 1998, DMG said it had slightly lowered its earnings per share outlook to 17 marks, from 18 marks.
DMG said it had lowered its forecast after a company visit, when it was told that restructuring costs would not fully hit the company until next year.
"The fact that problems of restructuring will go into next year was completely new for us," said one DMG building sector analyst.
The DMG building analysts said the company had operative problems in the German states of Thuringia and Saxony as well as in foreign subsidiaries including Austria and the Netherlands.
DMG said the recent sale of 4000 flats for a huge write-down of 350 million marks had been taken into account in the new forecast.
The group made losses of 443 million marks in 1995 following huge write-downs for losses on real estate projects.
DMG also said there were not yet any concrete plans or buyers for two Holzmann projects, which with which the company wanted to gain cash by a sale-and-lease back deal.
Shares in Holzmann touched a low of 360 marks on the news of the DMG forecast change and then recovered slightly to stand down 18 marks, over four percent, at 368 marks in a generally firmer market.
